'Q01':("1. Starting money: 25. 2. Workers: 1 active on the notepad and 3 inactive on the reserve spaces. 3. Zoo cards: draw 8, keep 4 and discard 4. 4. Final Scoring: draw 2. 5. Action cards: Animals goes in slot 1; the other four are randomly placed in the remaining slots; all begin side I up. 6. Starting appeal by turn order: first 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.","Personal setup: 25 money; 1 active and 3 reserve workers; draw 8/keep 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; Animals leftmost; appeal staggered by order."),
'Q02':("1. Base projects: with 4 players place the top 4 face up below the Association board; with 2 or 3 players place the top 3 face up there. 2. Two-player blocking: cover the left level of the left project, middle level of the middle project, right level of the right project, plus the three donation spaces in the left column; both players cannot use those spaces. 3. Three- and four-player games block none of those project levels or donation spaces at setup. 4. Reveal the initial 6-card display only after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.","Setup 5b–5c says 4 projects for four players, otherwise 3; only 2-player setup blocks the listed spaces; setup G reveals display after hand selection."),
'Q03':("1. After using the slot-4 card, remove it, shift the cards that were left of the empty slot one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set action strength before acting; each X-token spent then adds +1 strength and is returned to supply. X-tokens can raise strength for the current action, but those gained during that action cannot boost it. 3. Maximum held is 5 X-tokens. 4. Resolve an ‘after finishing’ effect after the action is complete, including moving Action cards.","Turn structure: remove used card; shift cards left of empty slot right; place used card in slot 1. X-tokens and after-finishing timing are stated under Turn Structure."),
'Q04':("1. You cannot take a regular action that does nothing: playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not legal. 2. Instead choose the X-token action: take exactly 1 X-token, while still selecting an Action card and moving it to slot 1 with the intervening cards shifted right; slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. 3. You cannot take it while holding 5 X-tokens.","Taking a turn forbids doing nothing; X-token action gives exactly one, moves the selected card, and is unavailable at five held."),
'Q05':("1. When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore steps beyond that space and gain 1 X-token. 2. The break occurs after the triggering player finishes the current turn. 3. Play then continues after the break with the next player clockwise; the summary’s break procedure says play continues clockwise with the next player.","Break track: last space calls a break after current turn, grants 1 X-token, ignores extra steps; break procedure resumes clockwise."),
'Q06':("1. Cards I always advances the Break token 2 spaces, then choose either deck draw per the strength table (maximum 3 cards, with any required discard) or snap exactly 1 display card at strength 5+. 2. Cards II also advances 2 spaces, then allows deck draws and/or display draws within reputation range in any order under its table; at strength 5 it draws 4 and discards 1. 3. Snap threshold is 5+ on I and 3+ on II; a snap takes exactly one display card, with no deck draw, and ignores reputation on either side. The reputation limit applies to Cards II’s display-draw option only. 4. Taken display cards are not replenished until turn end. 5. Hand limit is enforced at breaks only (3, or 5 with hand-limit university).","Cards action: sides I/II, thresholds and snap restriction; turn display timing and break hand limit."),
'Q07':("1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your reputation space and all lower-numbered folders. 2. Reputation 10 and above requires upgraded Cards. 3. At reputation 15, further reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 appeal per remaining reputation step. 4. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.","Reputation track and display defines range, Cards II gate, space-15 overflow, and discard-pile restriction."),
'Q08':("1. Build I builds exactly 1 building of size up to action strength. Build II builds as many different buildings as desired, total size no greater than strength; it cannot build two identical buildings in that action. 2. Pay 2 money per space before placing each building. 3. First building must include at least one map border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. 4. Build only on empty spaces; cannot overlap, leave the map, or cover water/rock. Restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 5. Each kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. 6. Each pavilion immediately gives 1 appeal once.","Build action gives I/II limits, cost, placement, restricted spaces, kiosk spacing and pavilion benefit."),
'Q09':("1. Build I permits standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo (size 3); standard enclosures and kiosks/pavilions may be built multiple times. 2. Build II additionally permits one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary per zoo (each size 5); it also permits restricted-icon spaces. 3. The component supply has four of each special enclosure, but each zoo may have only one of each special type. 4. Unique buildings cannot be built with Build; they enter through Sponsor cards. 5. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal, including when coverage comes from another building effect.","Building table and Build I/II; each zoo one of each special enclosure; unique building rule and full map reward."),
'Q10':("1. Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps in that same action; resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. 2. Immediate effects resolve at their stated point; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action and Action-card movement are complete. 3. If multiple effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.","Turn Structure says earlier bonuses may fund later steps and payment precedes own benefits; ‘after finishing’ and simultaneous effects rules."),
'Q11':("1. To play each animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its full cost, and house it legally; money-gain effects from the play occur only after you can pay the full cost. 2. A partner zoo matching a continent on the animal reduces cost by 3 money per such continent icon (so a double icon reduces it by 6). 3. Standard housing: an eligible animal needs one empty standard enclosure at least its printed minimum size; flip the whole enclosure to occupied. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. 4. Eligible reptiles and birds may use a Reptile House or Aviary if the alternative special-enclosure requirement fits; mark each occupied space with a supply player token and never flip the special enclosure. 5. Meet water/rock adjacency for the chosen enclosure; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not multiple edges to the same hex. 6. Advance appeal and resolve ordinary effects during the animal sequence; defer ‘after finishing’ effects until the whole Animals action ends and the Animals card moves. Resolve a first animal before a second, except deferred effects.","Animals action steps, partner discount, enclosure state/capacity, terrain, and effect timing."),
'Q12':("1. Animals II may play animals from display folders within reputation range, paying the folder number as additional cost; the display is not replenished until turn end. 2. At strength 5+, you may gain 1 reputation at the very start of the action, before selecting animals, so the increased range applies. 3. Animals II permits animals with the upgrade-required condition icon.","Animals II adds display source/folder cost, optional reputation first at strength 5+, and upgrade-conditioned animals."),
'Q13':("1. Existing animals may move only immediately when a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary is built, once per new building. Move any corresponding eligible animals that fit, choosing separately for each; total indicated special-space requirements must fit the new enclosure’s free capacity. 2. Add supply player tokens to the special enclosure, one for each required space. 3. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all its requirements, including terrain, to empty. If none meets all requirements, use the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting size alone; if none meets even size, flip none. This relocation does not remove the animal from your zoo.","Build II and relocation section: only immediately at construction; all suitable animals that fit; mark spaces with tokens; smallest-enclosure/fallback sequence."),
'Q14':("1. Task strengths: reputation 2; partner zoo 3; university 4; conservation project work 5. 2. Association I performs exactly one task, with strength at least its printed value. Association II may perform one or more different tasks with total task value no greater than action strength. 3. Each task uses 1 worker unless you already have one of your workers on that task, when you must place 2; with 3 already there you cannot repeat it until after break. 4. Other players’ workers on a task do not matter.","Association action: tasks and strengths; side I/II limits; repeated-task worker rule and other players’ workers."),
'Q15':("1. Take partner zoos and universities from available tiles on the Association board and place them on the lowest open matching spaces on your map; immediately resolve any covered map-space bonus. 2. You cannot take a duplicate university; partner zoos must be from different continents, maximum four. Third/fourth partner zoos require Association II. 3. University tiles also grant their printed reputation immediately; only the hand-limit university raises hand limit from 3 to 5. 4. Partner zoos provide their continent icon and reduce matching-continent animal costs by 3 per icon. A tile cannot be acquired if unavailable on the board.","Association task descriptions, zoo map columns, university details and hand-limit table."),
'Q16':("1. A Conservation Project can enter play from your hand and be supported immediately through Association work; Association II also permits a new card from display within reputation range, paying its folder number. Assertion/Dominance can obtain a base-project card from the unused face-down deck, which is later played and supported via Association above the board. 2. To support, fulfill a condition and choose a reward level with no player token on it; each level holds one token total, and normally you may support a given project only once. 3. Take one of your player tokens from the left edge of your zoo map and place it on that condition. Gain the project reward and activate the uncovered map bonus, in either order. 4. If a project above the board is pushed off by overflow, return its player tokens to their owners’ supplies; the map bonuses remain activated. Base projects below never move.","Association project work, support procedure and limits, token origin, reward/map bonus order, and overflow handling."),
'Q17':("1. Release project size categories must match the animal’s printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− accepts size 1 or 2; 3 accepts exactly size 3; 4+ accepts 4 or 5. They are not based on the actual enclosure or special-enclosure capacity. 2. Lose only the animal’s printed appeal before gaining conservation; discard the animal and lose its icons. Retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects already earned. 3. Playing a new Release project grants 1 reputation; later supporting it does not. 4. If the released animal could use a special enclosure and its required tokens can be removed, remove those tokens; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, or the smallest meeting size alone as fallback, or none if none meets size.","Release into the wild procedure: exact printed size category, losses/retained rewards, project play reputation, housing release/fallback."),
'Q18':("1. Sponsors I: play exactly 1 Sponsor from hand; strength must be at least its level and all conditions must be met. Alternatively advance the Break token by action strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II: play one or more cards whose total levels are at most action strength +1; X-tokens can raise strength beyond 5. Use hand and/or display within reputation range, pay each display folder number, and refill only at turn end. Resolve cards one by one, fully completing each instant effect before the next; defer after-finishing effects. 3. If choosing the break/money option on Sponsors II, advance the Break token and take money twice the action strength, even if only one space remains before the last space.","Sponsors I/II rules state level budgets, card sources/cost/refill, effect order, and doubled money option; break excess is ignored but full money is paid."),
'Q19':("1. Break order: discard down to hand limit; clear Multiplier/Venom/Constriction tokens; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1–2, compact and refill; take income; reset Break token. 2. Hand limit is 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university. 3. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion. Empty standard enclosures do not qualify; empty special enclosures do. 4. When multiple players take display cards during income, resolve affected players clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), refilling the display after each such player before the next chooses.","Break procedure steps and kiosk income; explicit between-player display refill/order rule."),
'Q20':("1. At 2 conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate one additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or an available Bonus tile; execute tile immediately and remove it. At 10, the first player to reach/pass it makes all players discard one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if nobody reaches 10, everyone discards one before scoring. 2. Check end at end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. If appeal is gained on another player’s turn, the receiving zoo checks at the end of its own turn or during a break. 3. Triggering player completes their turn and each other player gets one more; a break trigger gives every player one more turn. 4. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation. VP equals appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; tie goes to most supported projects, then shared victory.","Conservation milestones; end timing/trigger/last turns; final scoring cap, formula and tiebreak."),
'Q21':("1. Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles; place one random tile face up on each of the four blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track (two at 5 and two at 8); do not use the two yellow spaces with icons. Return the remaining five to the box. 2. Components are not limited by physical stock: use a suitable substitute if a component runs out, while honoring explicit per-zoo limits and Association-board availability rules.","Setup bonus tiles; component supply rule says use suitable substitute, with explicit limits still applying."),
'Q22':("1. Advanced Maps 1–8: either take 2 random zoo maps and choose one advanced map, or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose in reverse turn order. 2. Map A starts with an empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on the indicated spaces; the printed kiosk counts as built, with a kiosk tile placed over it as reminder.","Personal setup A gives advanced map selection methods and Map A starting buildings."),
'Q23':("1. The seven player tokens begin on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; the rest stay beside the map. 2. Hire/activate reserve workers from the lowest remaining space upward. 3. Certain maps give conservation points when you hire your last worker; Full-throated also directs you to take that map reward.","Personal setup C2; Association worker supply and Full-throated clarification."),
'Q24':("1. Flip one chosen side-I Action card to side II in its current slot; it does not move. 2. Its improved action is usable starting with your next action, but the card counts as upgraded immediately for conditions. 3. You cannot upgrade all five Action cards; one upgrade source allows an alternative choice, so not every card can be upgraded.","Upgrade Action cards: remains in slot; next-action use; immediate condition status; four paths and limitation."),
'Q25':("1. Cards I deck draws by strength 1–5: draw 1/discard 1; 1/0; 2/1; 2/0; 3/1. 2. A required discard may be one of the cards just drawn or a card already in your hand.","Cards draw tables; required discard may be new or previously held."),
'Q28':("1. The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear, and Petting Zoo animal. 2. Bear remains a category even when it appears with herbivore or predator; Petting Zoo animal is its own category. Count both special categories unless the effect explicitly excludes them.","Base glossary names all seven categories and clarifies bear and Petting Zoo animal."),
'Q29':("1. Donations are Association II only; the card must be upgraded and you must have performed at least one association task in that same action. No worker is needed for the donation; maximum one donation per Association action. 2. Pay the smallest amount still visible in the donation area, cover it with one player token from your supply, and gain 1 conservation. 3. Printed ladder: 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then repeatable 12. Skip spaces blocked at setup. 4. Once all spaces but the last are covered, each later donation costs 12 and places no further token.","Donations section gives eligibility, payment, supply token/reward, ladder and repeatable final space."),
'Q30':("1. Count upper-right icons on Animal and Sponsor cards; for Animal cards and unique-building Sponsor cards also count upper-left water/rock requirements. Count partner-zoo continent icons and university research icons. 2. Do not count left-side play conditions, conservation-project icons, university reputation award or hand-limit mark as zoo icons. 3. A card counts its own icons for effects; doubled icons count twice and trigger twice, but repeated icons count only once when an effect asks for different types. 4. Card text takes priority over general rules.","Glossary counting-icons rules and card-text priority."),
'Q31':("1. A requirement for two water/rock spaces means two distinct adjacent terrain hexes; multiple touching edges to one hex count as one. A larger terrain region counts only the individual hexes adjacent to the enclosure. 2. Connected terrain regions do not make distant hexes count as adjacent. 3. Water/rock illustrations printed on tiles are decorative and are not terrain spaces or requirements.","Terrain adjacency counts distinct hexes; tile illustrations provide neither terrain spaces nor requirements."),
'Q32':("1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project gives 1 reputation to the player who brings it into play; supporting it later gives no such play bonus. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same condition at all three reward levels; once satisfied, choose any available reward space rather than matching different conditions to different levels.","Release project rule; all Breeding Program cards use same condition on all levels and allow any available space."),
'Q33':("1. In X:Y, X is the condition and Y is the reward. 2. If the condition has no number or says ‘per,’ gain the reward once per fulfillment. 3. A numbered threshold pays only once; with several thresholds, use the highest one met.","Glossary X:Y rule."),
'Q34':("1. Connected space: uncovered and shares an edge with a covered space. 2. Isolated space: has no adjacent covered space. 3. Border space: lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of its six sides. 4. ‘Your zoo’ includes your played cards, map and personal supply. 5. ‘Any zoo’ includes those components for every player.","Glossary definitions of connected, isolated, border, your zoo and any zoo."),
'Q35':("1. Unique buildings enter through their Sponsor and must be placed when that Sponsor is played; if placement is impossible, the card cannot be played. 2. No size-based construction payment is due. Use the matching tile, colored face up; it may be rotated freely but not flipped. 3. Follow ordinary placement and terrain rules. Unique buildings are not enclosures, cannot house extra animals, and never count as water or rock spaces.","Unique building glossary rules."),
'Q36':("1. For either Named Action or Determination, finish the Animals action and move the Animals card to slot 1 before taking the granted action. 2. Use the granted action’s Action card normally, then move that card to slot 1 after the granted action. 3. A named action cannot be replaced with the X-token action; Determination (Any Action) may choose any action, including X-token.","Action/Determination clarification gives shared timing, card movement and distinction on X-token action."),
'Q37':("1. Search the unused face-down base-project deck and take the chosen project (Assertion) or named project (Dominance) into hand; return the deck. 2. Dominance has no effect if its named project is already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support the acquired project through Association, placing it above the board, not in the base-project row below.","Assertion/Dominance clarification."),
'Q38':("1. Resolve Boost/Clever after finishing Animals and moving that card. 2. Clever moves the selected card to slot 1; cards formerly to its left shift right. 3. Boost moves the named card to slot 1 or 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.","Boost/Clever clarification."),
'Q39':("1. Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering 1, each separate Pilfering 2 target, and Constriction require each affected zoo to have at least 5 appeal. Apply the floor separately to every selected zoo. 2. The playing animal’s appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so its new appeal normally need not count for choosing targets. 3. Multiplayer groups may use the alternative text marked for solo on those cards without playing solo mode.","Interactive abilities shared eligibility and self-selection rules."),
'Q40':("1. Each affected other zoo places Constriction tokens on its own Action cards: if ahead on one track, one token on its slot-5 card; if ahead on both, one each on its slot-4 and slot-5 cards. 2. Do not stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. 3. Each affected action loses 2 strength, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. 4. Return the token after acting, or without effect at the break.","Constriction rules state target card ownership, slot placement, no stacking, strength loss and removal."),
'Q41':("1. A constricted card in slot 1 or 2 has effective strength below 1; you cannot use a regular action at zero or below. 2. You may spend enough X-tokens to reach at least strength 1, use the alternative X-token action, or leave that card unused until it is at least in slot 3. The alternative X-token action is possible only if you hold fewer than five X-tokens.","Constriction: at effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens, alternative X-token action, or leave until slot 3; X action cap."),
'Q42':("1. Yes. Digging offers up to two choices and you decide again after each card which option to use. 2. If you discard a display card through Digging, replace it immediately, shifting higher folders down and drawing into folder 6.","Digging 2 clarification."),
'Q43':("1. A flock animal may avoid a new enclosure if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal’s standard-enclosure size. 2. The same qualifying herbivore may host any number of flock animals. 3. Without such a host, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. 4. When releasing a flock animal, free an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure even if it shared; exact historical residents need not be tracked.","Flock Animal clarification."),
'Q44':("1. Full-throated activates the lowest remaining reserve worker by moving it onto the notepad for immediate use. 2. Take any conservation-point reward printed on your map for hiring your last worker. 3. If all workers are active, the ability has no effect.","Full-throated clarification."),
'Q45':("1. If Hunter reveals no Animal card, discard all revealed cards; add no card to hand.","Hunter X clarification."),
'Q46':("1. If multiple zoos tie for highest appeal, the acting player chooses the target; if the acting player is selected, Hypnosis has no effect. 2. Target only a card in slot 1, 2 or 3. Copy it using its owner’s upgraded/unupgraded side for the whole action; other action-card upgrade checks use your own cards. You may spend your own X-tokens. 3. Move the copied card to slot 1 normally. 4. Venom and Constriction on it apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.","Hypnosis rules on ties/self, slots, card side, X-tokens, movement and tokens."),
'Q49':("1. A Multiplier gained from a reward naming an Action card goes on that card; one from a Bonus tile may go on any Action card, including Animals. 2. On its next use you may execute the action twice in succession at the same base strength and move the card only after both. Each X-token boosts only one execution. 3. Defer after-finishing effects until all executions finish. A break caused by the first waits until the entire turn ends; it does not stop the second execution. 4. Return used tokens to supply; an unused token is removed at the next break.","Multiplier placement/execution/X-token/timing/return rules."),
'Q50':("1. Two Multiplier tokens allow up to three executions total, not four. 2. A multiplied X-token alternative may take two X-tokens, subject to the five-token cap, but cannot mix an X-token action with a regular action.","Multiplier additional-token and choices rules."),
'Q51':("1. Peacocking permits placing a Large Bird Aviary before Build II, provided your zoo has no Aviary and a legal site exists. 2.
